- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast peak values.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly bearish (≤-0.33) or mixed, particularly if recent prices are trending downward; adjust downward bias.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves (e.g., >70.00) — cap forecast peaks at 5–10% below recent high if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- Lagged overreaction: if forecast is >10% above true outcome 3–5 days prior, adjust downward by 1–3% to avoid echo effect.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is negative or mixed over last 5 days; increase if sentiment is consistently positive.
- Avoid “sentiment echo”: if sentiment is positive but price is falling, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence in sentiment-driven momentum.
